evidence: The PR changes js/apps/admin-ui/maven-resources/theme/keycloak.v2/admin/messages/messages_en.properties:3138 and js/apps/account-ui/maven-resources/theme/keycloak.v3/account/messages/messages_en.properties:188 from {{0}}/{{1}}/{{2}} to Java MessageFormat syntax: {0} ... {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}. Both UIs load bundles through i18next (js/apps/admin-ui/src/i18n/i18n.ts:13-33, js/apps/account-ui/src/i18n.ts:25-41). The server returns the raw properties with no format conversion (services/.../ThemeResource.java:118-157). Server errors are rendered with t(key, {...params}) (js/libs/ui-shared/src/user-profile/utils.ts:73-85), and i18next only interpolates {{n}}. So the UIs would show '{0}' and the literal choice pattern. Sibling keys in the same admin file still use {{0}} (messages_en.properties:2989-2994). The theme-side files (themes/.../base/admin|login/messages_en.properties) are rendered by Java MessageFormat, so the change is correct only there.

misc/theme-verifier/pom.xml:76-79 adds owasp-java-html-sanitizer 20240325.1. That is the same version the root build manages (pom.xml:119 owasp.html.sanitizer.version=20240325.1), and it was the latest release when the PR was made (HEAD commit date 2025-02-18). The suggested 20260313.1 did not exist then. A routine version bump is not a defect in this PR and can be done separately. Keeping it aligned with the root pom is the better choice.

misc/theme-verifier/pom.xml:80-85 adds commons-text 1.13.0, which was the current release when the PR was made (2025-02-18). The suggested 1.15.0 came later. This is a standalone build-time maven plugin with no parent pom (misc/theme-verifier/pom.xml:22-29), and it only uses StringEscapeUtils.unescapeHtml4 (VerifyMessageProperties.java:93,132). Being 'outdated' is not a defect here.

themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/account/messages/messages_lt.properties:101: the PR replaces the Lithuanian 'Įdiekite FreeOTP arba Google Authenticator...' with the Italian 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:'. The rest of the file, including totpStep2/3 at lines 102-103, is Lithuanian. Lithuanian users would see Italian text. It should be a Lithuanian translation, e.g. 'Įdiekite vieną iš šių programėlių savo mobiliajame telefone:'.

themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/account/messages/messages_zh_CN.properties:112: the PR introduces '在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：', which uses Traditional forms (手機, 安裝, 應用程式). The rest of the zh_CN bundle is Simplified, e.g. mobile=手机 at line 111. The zh_CN login bundle already has a Simplified equivalent: loginTotpStep1=在您的移动设备中安装以下任意一个应用： (login/messages/messages_zh_CN.properties:123).

themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/login/messages/messages_lt.properties:71: the PR replaces the Lithuanian loginTotpStep1 with the Italian 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:'. The neighbouring loginTotpStep2/3 at lines 72-73 are Lithuanian. Lithuanian users would see Italian on the OTP setup login page.

misc/theme-verifier/src/main/java/org/keycloak/themeverifier/VerifyMessageProperties.java:87 and :150: the private method is named santizeAnchors, a misspelling of sanitizeAnchors. It is private, so there is no API impact and the rename is a trivial readability fix.

VerifyMessageProperties.java:58-63: POLICY_SOME_HTML and POLICY_NO_HTML are package-private instance fields with UPPER_CASE constant-style names. ThemeVerifierMojo.java:51 creates a new VerifyMessageProperties for each properties file, so both policies are rebuilt per file. PolicyFactory is immutable and thread-safe, so they can be private static final. The same file already does this for ANCHOR_PATTERN (line 145). This only affects a build-time tool, so the gain is small.

VerifyMessageProperties.java:137: 'Pattern HTML_TAGS = Pattern.compile(...)' is an instance field, so it is recompiled for each file checked (ThemeVerifierMojo.java:51 creates one instance per file). ANCHOR_PATTERN at line 145 is already private static final. Making HTML_TAGS match is a small consistency and performance improvement in a build-time tool.
